reason: Never reached a responsive live-gameplay state within a reasonable probe budget. Two independent probes agree: (1) a short boot-mash (STARTx2, A, START; 446 sim-steps, 1784 emulated frames) followed by a 120-frame input-divergence probe (RIGHT/LEFT/A/NOOP held independently from the same reload) came back nearly input-invariant -- RIGHT-vs-LEFT diverges only 5/2048 RAM bytes, RIGHT-vs-NOOP 5 bytes, LEFT-vs-NOOP 4 bytes, A-vs-NOOP 4 bytes -- the same signature as a scripted/non-interactive screen (compare Power Blade's confirmed-inert 2/2048, and Blaster Master/Paperboy's confirmed-live 46-401+ byte divergences on the identical method). (2) A much longer probe -- periodic START presses (20 held-frames every 120) sustained across 7200 sim-steps / 28,800 emulated frames (~480s emulated at 60fps, ~72s wall) -- shows a persistent, UNCHANGING steady-state RAM churn of ~440-460 bytes per 100-frame window from step ~600 onward, with no transition to a lower-churn idle/title state and no qualitative change from additional START presses anywhere in the window. This matches an ongoing scripted intro/attract sequence (likely the game's well-known unskippable opening cinematic and/or a title-screen demo loop) that keeps animating on its own script regardless of input, not a game that is merely slow to reach its title screen. No start state was banked (no roms/Castlevania III - Dracula's Curse (USA)_start.state.bin file was written) so a non-interactive state is not forced through the odometer gate or solver smoke.

liveness_probe.method: save state after boot-mash; reload into a fresh pool; hold RIGHT/LEFT/A/NOOP independently for 120 frames each; diff full 2KB RAM pairwise

probe_2_extended_boot_trace.method: repeat (START held 20 frames, settle 100 frames) x60 blocks = 7200 sim-steps / 28,800 emulated frames; log RAM-diff between consecutive 100-frame checkpoints
probe_2_extended_boot_trace.churn_pattern: diff stabilizes to a narrow 438-478 byte/100-frame band by step ~600 and never leaves that band through step 7200 (~480s emulated game time), regardless of the periodic START presses

conclusion: mint_failed -- boot-mash candidate is non-interactive (near-zero input divergence) and an 8-minutes-of-emulated-time extended probe never breaks out of the same steady-state churn pattern regardless of additional START presses. Classifying as an unskippable scripted intro/demo loop rather than forcing this state into the odometer gate / solver smoke, per the task's stop condition.
